exact_statement: For every balanced Boolean h on n<=4 uniform bits, and every antipodally odd Boolean h on n=5, Lambda(h)<=3 ln(2)(I(h)-1). The maximum ratio for non-dictators is 3 ln(2) for n=3,4 and odd n=5. All 224 n=4 equality tables form two NPN orbits: 32 Maj3 juntas and 192 variants of h that returns x3 if x3=x4, otherwise x1 when x3=+1 and x2 when x3=-1; this h has H=3, I=3/2 and singleton coefficients (1/4,1/4,1/2,1/2). For every even m>=2, d=2^-m, paired quadratic bent b, D=1_(y=0), g_m=D+z(b-D), and 0<x<1, 0<B_z(g_m)-L_z(x)<=d log2(1/x). For even m>=4, L_z(x)/B_z(g_m)>=1-log2(1/x)/m. Consequently for every 0<c<1 the supremum L_j(alpha^2)/B_j(g) over genuine balanced-child disjoint compositions with B_j(g)>0 and |alpha|<=1-c is 1; this also admits a sequence alpha->0. The cap coefficient 1 survives disjoint outer tensor products and cannot be reduced using a fixed additive overhead. In contrast, Lambda of a product of two balanced functions is zero and is not tensor additive.

exact_statement: Let F=g(h_1,...,h_m) on pairwise disjoint blocks of independent uniform signs, g Boolean on m bits, every h_k Boolean and balanced. Fix a coordinate i in block j; write a_T=ghat(T), b_T=ghat(T+{j}) for T not containing j, q=Inf_j(g)=sum_T b_T^2, alpha=hhat_j({i}), phi(u,v)=(u+v)ln(u+v)-u ln u-v ln v and L_j(x)=sum_T phi(a_T^2, x b_T^2) (nats). Then L_j is nondecreasing and concave on [0,1] with L_j'(x)=sum_T b_T^2 ln(1+a_T^2/(x b_T^2)) and L_j(1)=B_j(g); hence L_j(alpha^2) <= min{B_j(g), alpha^2 B_j(g)+q alpha^2 ln(1/alpha^2)} and, by the A057 erasure split, B_i(F) <= q B_i(h_j) + min{B_j(g), alpha^2 B_j(g)+q alpha^2 ln(1/alpha^2)}.
